name: John Donne

source.title: The Poems of John Donne, Volume 1
source.edition: Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1912, volume 1 (the text; volume 2 is commentary and is not used). Keeps the spelling of the 1633 printing. Public domain.
source.note: Ingest starts at Songs and Sonets, ends at Appendix A, and drops unindented lines (italic titles); the bracketed textual apparatus is removed by the bracket rules.

voice: Argument as passion. A poem is a case being made to one listener, a lover or God, with a conceit pushed further than seems reasonable: compasses, a flea, maps, new worlds, a tear. Start in the middle of the quarrel. Rough stresses, abrupt openings, a close that clinches. The spelling here is the 1633 printing's, so 'starre' and 'goe' and 'bee' are his words; use them without apology and do not modernize them.
